title: "00 · Setup"
subtitle: "Run once per computer"
execute:
  eval: false   # run these chunks by hand; `quarto render` skips them
---

Run each chunk below **one at a time**. Re-running is
safe: Step 1 skips anything already installed.

## Step 1 · Install packages

```{r}
# Packages from CRAN, grouped by what they're for.
cran_packages <- c(
  "here", "remotes", "BiocManager",            # project tools
  "ebirdst",                                   # eBird Status & Trends data
  "terra", "sf", "maps",                       # spatial data
  "dplyr", "tidyr", "readr", "purrr",          # data wrangling
  "lubridate", "ggplot2", "gganimate", "gifski",
  "rnaturalearthdata",                         # basemaps used by BirdFlowR
  "vol2birdR", "bioRad"                        # weather radar
)

# Install only what's missing.
missing <- setdiff(cran_packages, rownames(installed.packages()))
if (length(missing) > 0) install.packages(missing)

# rhdf5 reads BirdFlow model files. It comes from Bioconductor, not CRAN.
if (!"rhdf5" %in% rownames(installed.packages())) {
  BiocManager::install("rhdf5", update = FALSE, ask = FALSE)
}

# BirdFlowR isn't on CRAN yet, so we install it from GitHub.
# If R asks about updating other packages, press Enter to skip.
if (!"BirdFlowR" %in% rownames(installed.packages())) {
  remotes::install_github("birdflow-science/BirdFlowR")
}
```

If the BirdFlowR line fails with **"HTTP error 401 / Bad credentials"**, R is
sending an old GitHub login. This installs it without one:

```{r}
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".tar.gz")
download.file("https://codeload.github.com/birdflow-science/BirdFlowR/tar.gz/refs/heads/main",
              tmp, mode = "wb")
remotes::install_local(tmp)
```

## Step 2 · Save your eBird key

Each user needs their **own** key from <https://ebird.org/st/request>.
Never paste it into a file in this project.

```{r}
# Paste your key into the Console when asked. It's saved in a settings file
# in your home folder (~/.Renviron), outside this project.
ebirdst::set_ebirdst_access_key(readline("Paste your eBird key: "))
```

Then restart R: **Session → Restart R**.

## Step 3 · Check everything works

```{r}
# 1. Is the key loaded? Should print TRUE (the key itself is never shown).
nchar(Sys.getenv("EBIRDST_KEY")) > 0

# 2. Are all packages installed? Should print character(0).
needed <- c("ebirdst", "terra", "sf", "maps", "dplyr", "ggplot2",
            "bioRad", "vol2birdR", "rhdf5", "BirdFlowR")
setdiff(needed, rownames(installed.packages()))

# 3. Which eBird data version? Should say 2023 (matches our citation).
ebirdst::ebirdst_version()$status_version_year

# 4. Test download: a small example dataset. Should print a raster with 52 layers.
ebirdst::ebirdst_download_status("yebsap-example")
ebirdst::load_raster("yebsap-example", resolution = "27km")

# 5. Record your package versions so the team can compare if results differ.
pkgs <- installed.packages()[needed, "Version"]
readr::write_csv(data.frame(package = names(pkgs), version = pkgs),
                 here::here("package_versions.csv"))
```
